story.headline: For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
story.summary: Full-fat dairy may not be the health villain it has long been portrayed as, according to a new study finding that three daily servings did not worsen weight, cholesterol, or insulin resistance over 12 weeks. story.score_reason: Full-fat dairy myth, practical food choice

carousel.cover_headline:
Full-Fat Dairy Was Blamed
For Decades.
New Research Disagrees.

slides.label: THE STUDY
slides.headline: 74 adults ate full-fat dairy for **12 weeks**
slides.insight: Weight, cholesterol, and insulin resistance did not worsen.

slides.label: WHAT THEY FOUND
slides.headline: Three daily servings — no harmful changes observed
slides.insight: Blood pressure and nutrient intake actually improved in dairy group.

slides.label: OLD THINKING
slides.headline: Saturated fat in dairy raised one concern: LDL cholesterol
slides.insight: That shaped decades of low-fat dairy advice in many countries.

slides.label: BIGGER PICTURE
slides.headline: Dairy foods may behave differently than saturated fat alone suggests
slides.insight: Researchers say the health effects of dairy are more complicated.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Check what dairy you buy — full-fat or low-fat?
slides.insight: Read the label. Notice the difference. Talk to your doctor before changing.

sources: University of Toronto / Harvey Anderson et al., The Journal of Nutrition, 2026 (reported by ScienceDaily)
carousel.caption:
Full-Fat Dairy Was Blamed For Decades. New Research Disagrees.

A Canadian study of 74 adults found that three servings of full-fat dairy daily for 12 weeks did not worsen weight, cholesterol, or insulin resistance — and blood pressure actually improved in that group.
Researchers say the health effects of dairy may be more complicated than saturated fat alone suggests.
What dairy do you usually buy — full-fat or low-fat, and why?

Not medical advice.

Sources: University of Toronto / Harvey Anderson et al., The Journal of Nutrition, 2026 (reported by ScienceDaily)
